claims.text: Data-driven or machine-learning-guided optimization can be used to explore the non-equiatomic compositional space of HEAs.
The initial material is a non-equiatomic HEA made by conventional synthesis without targeted compositional tuning.
The optimization approach systematically adjusts elemental ratios in the alloy.
The relevant measurements should be performed near the magnetic phase-transition temperatures.
Interfacial and size effects matter under the proposed low-dimensional constraints.
Optimized non-uniform elemental compositions produce tailored local chemical ordering.
Optimized non-uniform elemental compositions modulate local magnetic exchange interactions.
The machine-learning model can identify non-intuitive compositional adjustments.
The identified compositional adjustments optimize local magnetic moments and their coupling.
Tuning local magnetic moments and their coupling shifts magnetic phase-transition temperatures.
Tuning local magnetic moments and their coupling enhances the magnetic entropy change.
ML-guided HEAs will have a larger magnetic entropy change than conventionally designed baseline samples.
ML-guided HEAs will have a tunable magnetic transition temperature.
The larger entropy change and tunable transition temperature will improve magnetocaloric efficiency.
Standard equiatomic or non-ML-guided non-equiatomic HEAs have shown only limited tuning of magnetic entropy change.
The expected improvements are restricted to low-dimensional systems and the explored non-equiatomic compositional range.
The enhancement magnitude and optimal elemental adjustments remain uncertain pending systematic experiments.
Magnetic entropy change can be determined from magnetization and temperature sweeps.
Magnetic transition temperature can be determined through susceptibility measurements.
A controlled comparison under identical thermal and magnetic-field protocols can test whether ML-guided compositions improve magnetic entropy change and transition-temperature control.
